summary: Restoration is EU-level: by 2030, measures should cover at least 20% of EU land and sea areas—20% of Czechia’s land is about 15,758 km², with no national allocation stated—and by 2050 all ecosystems needing restoration should have measures in place. Conservation focuses on LULUCF, with a Union 2030 accounting target of −310 Mt CO2-eq (310 Mt of net removals and 42 Mt above the 2016–2018 average) and a Czechia target of −827 kt CO2eq using that baseline. Combined restoration and conservation have EU mitigation potentials of 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr from peatland and wetland restoration and 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr from ecologically sound reforestation and sustainable forest management. Agriculture includes improved fertiliser-use efficiency, rated at 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr. No Czechian area allocation is stated: forest, grassland, wetland and agriculture cover 37.4%, 8.4%, 0.1% and 50.0%, respectively.
